title: Tail transition factorizations bound tensor kernels of colimit maps
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $I$ be a small nonempty directed partially ordered set, and let $(M_s,f_{st})_{s\in I}$ be a directed system of $R$-modules with colimit $M$ and canonical maps $f_s:M_s\to M$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Fix $i,j\in I$ with $i\le j$. Assume that for every $k\ge j$ there exists an $R$-linear map $h_k:M_k\to M_j$ such that $h_k\circ f_{ik}=f_{ij}$. Then for every $R$-module $L$ one has $\ker(f_i\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L)\subseteq\ker(f_{ij}\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L)$ as submodules of $M_i\otimes_RL$. Tensor products and their induced maps are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. No finite-presentation or Mittag-Leffler hypothesis on these modules is imposed.

source.place: Tag 059E (proposition-ML-characterization), (3) implies (2), tensor-kernel union and factorization argument; tail-only version.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary $R$-module $L$. Put $T_s=M_s\otimes_R L$, $t_{st}=f_{st}\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L$, and $u_s=f_s\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-commutes-with-colimits], $(M\otimes_R L,(u_s)_s)$ is a colimit of the diagram $(T_s,t_{st})$. This applies to the given colimit cocone, so its legs are exactly the maps occurring in the asserted kernel inclusion.

source.place: Tag 059E (proposition-ML-characterization), proof of (3) implies (2); tail-only adaptation using Tags 00DD and 00D7.

proof.text: Let $z\in\ker(u_i)$. The nonempty directed poset $I$ is a small filtered category. Apply the zero-detection clause of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] to the tensor-module colimit from step 1. There are $k_0\ge i$ with $t_{i k_0}(z)=0$. This clause applies to arbitrary modules, so no finite-presentation or flatness hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 059E (proposition-ML-characterization), proof of (3) implies (2); tail-only adaptation using Tags 00DD and 00D7.

proof.text: Choose a common upper bound $k\ge k_0,j$ using directedness. Tensor functoriality [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and the system identity $f_{ik}=f_{k_0 k}\circ f_{i k_0}$ give $t_{ik}(z)=t_{k_0 k}(t_{i k_0}(z))=t_{k_0 k}(0)=0$. Thus the zero witness can always be chosen in the tail on which the hypothesis supplies factorizations.

source.place: Tag 059E (proposition-ML-characterization), proof of (3) implies (2); tail-only adaptation using Tags 00DD and 00D7.

proof.text: Since $k\ge j$, choose the assumed $R$-linear map $h_k:M_k\to M_j$ with $h_k\circ f_{ik}=f_{ij}$. By compatibility of tensor maps with composition [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], $t_{ij}(z)=(h_k\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L)(t_{ik}(z))=(h_k\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L)(0)=0$. Hence every $z\in\ker(u_i)$ lies in $\ker(t_{ij})$. Since $L$ was arbitrary, this is the asserted inclusion for every $R$-module $L$.
